HRA Exemption Formula

Exempt HRA = lowest of:
1. HRA actually received
2. Rent paid − 10% of salary
3. 50% of salary (listed cities) or 40% of salary (others)

Example: You live in Bengaluru in FY 2026-27, with ₹60,000 a month in basic pay, ₹24,000 in HRA and ₹25,000 in rent. Over the year, your HRA is ₹2,88,000, your rent minus 10% of salary is ₹2,28,000, and 50% of salary is ₹3,60,000. The lowest gives ₹2,28,000 exempt and ₹60,000 taxable.

In this example, the move to 50% changes nothing, because the rent test is lower. The new limit only helps renters paying a high rent compared with their salary.

How to Use This Calculator

  1. Enter your monthly basic pay plus DA from your payslip
  2. Enter the HRA you receive and the rent you pay each month
  3. Choose your city group and the financial year
  4. Check the exempt amount, and which of the three limits sets it

If your salary or rent changed during the year, the rules work month by month, so run each period separately and add up the results.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is HRA exemption calculated?
It is the lowest of three amounts: the HRA you actually received, the rent you paid minus 10% of your salary, or a percentage of your salary set by your city. Salary here means basic pay plus any dearness allowance that counts for retirement benefits.
Which cities get the 50% HRA limit?
Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai have long been at 50%. From FY 2026-27, the Income-tax Rules, 2026 are reported to add Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad. Other cities are at 40%. For FY 2025-26, those four new cities remain at 40%.
Can I claim HRA under the new tax regime?
No. HRA exemption is only available under the old regime. Under the new regime, the whole allowance is taxable, so compare both regimes before you choose.
Do I need my landlord's PAN to claim HRA?
Employers generally ask for your landlord's PAN when your rent is above ₹1 lakh a year. Keep your rent receipts and rental agreement too, since you may need them if your claim is questioned.
Can I claim HRA if I pay rent to my parents?
Generally yes, if the rent is genuine and paid to a parent who owns the home. They should report it as income, and you should keep records of payment. A claim for rent paid to a spouse is much more likely to be challenged.
